title: 956. Powerful Integers

examples.explanation: The sums 2^i + 3^j within bound are 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 10 (order does not matter).
Reachable sums are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14; everything else overshoots the bound.
Since 1^j is always 1, the sums are 2, 3, 5 and 9.

hints: Loop over powers of x and, nested inside, powers of y, keeping sums within bound.
A base of 1 never grows — take its single power and move on to avoid an infinite loop.
Deduplicate with a set; order is irrelevant to the judge.
